overall_assessment:
Local-source test-quality conclusion: no new material defect was found in the cp36i test-only delta. The added revoked-grant unit case directly exercises the existing production guard and is effective, efficient, and non-brittle. This is only a local private-source audit result; it does not complete the delivery, waive D-06/VAL-05, replace the distinct final-review gate, or establish a fresh full-suite/browser/runtime claim.

Audit frame and inspection: read-only review; no tests, builds, runtime/provider/network actions, Git-wide inspection, private dotenv/cookie/operator data, .local-files, or dispatch contents were accessed. Readiness and formal-review routing preflight passed. I independently inspected all nine current public paths: api-app/src/domain/channels/channels.service.ts, api-app/src/domain/channels/receipt-attempt-convergence.ts, api-app/src/surfaces/webhooks/evolution.controller.ts, api-app/src/integrations/meta/meta.client.ts, api-app/src/integrations/meta/meta.client.spec.ts, api-app/test/number-onboarding-flow.e2e-spec.ts, api-app/test/helpers.ts, api-app/test/browser-server.cjs, and web-app/e2e/telas.spec.ts; plus the public DI, controller, credential-resolver, runner, build, Playwright, TODO, module, and indexed-evidence guards needed to judge them.

Five required answers:

1. Product/contract alignment: yes. The sole cp36i source delta is meta.client.spec.ts. Its revoked but otherwise valid-shaped grant at lines 175-207 checks the real existing invariant in meta.client.ts:94-100 and the persisted-number verification path at lines 154-173. It is correctly a coverage remediation for existing D-05/D-07 behavior, not a fictional product change.
2. Pass-the-test or brittle-shortcut risk: no material indication. The test does not alter production code, fixture/runner behavior, or routes. It supplies a valid fallback phone page, then proves it is never reached through exactly one fetch and no phone-number URL. If the is_valid guard or its pre-page short circuit regressed, the assertion would fail.
3. Assertion efficacy: strong. It checks typed error class and catalog code, exact Graph origin/path, scoped candidate input token, app credential header, exact call count, and zero downstream lookup. Existing BFF/PG evidence separately proves that actual MetaHttpClient failures become the fixed safe 503 while generic failures remain generic.
4. Assertion efficiency: strong. One targeted unit branch closes the identified semantic-false gap without duplicating a BFF case that already tests the same typed-error seam. Production remains bounded to one grant lookup plus at most two phone pages, 10-second request timeout, and a 45-second lease; this audit makes no capacity or SLO claim.
5. Coverage sufficiency: sufficient for the new local regression target when combined with the nearby adapter, BFF/PG, lease, tenant, ownership, epoch, webhook, browser-harness, and UI evidence. It is not sufficient for real Meta/device/Evolution recovery proof; that remains the high-severity external blocker.

Architecture, code-quality, test, performance, and security framing: the unit targets the actual adapter rather than a duplicate parser. BffModule binds META_CLIENT to MetaHttpClient at bff.module.ts:95-100, while helpers.ts:163-176 overrides that exact production token in Nest; number-onboarding-flow.e2e-spec.ts:151-224 deliberately bridges that token to the real adapter for malformed-response/typed-mapper proof. browser-server.cjs imports the built MetaIndisponivelError rather than recreating it. ChannelCredentialResolver resolves the current verified channel credential and fails closed; no production Meta fallback to a global customer token was observed. ChannelsService catches only MetaIndisponivelError for the fixed safe envelope at lines 281-354 and preserves generic/auth/CAS errors. Fixed Graph host, redirect:error, bounded opaque cursors, scoped credential/AAD, lease fencing, receipt convergence, CSRF, durable owner/tombstone, and no-GET-mutation boundaries remain represented in the named source and test layers.

Fail-first/test-after assessment: cp36i is explicitly test-after because production behavior was already correct and only H01 coverage was missing. It is not retrofit-risk: the assertion is discriminating against the exact false-validity branch, and no invented RED history is claimed. The supplied history preserves prior genuine RED evidence where it existed and does not relabel this test-only change as a bugfix.

Bypass, fallback, and DI-parity assessment: targeted static review found no focused/skipped tests, golden-update path, retry/sleep masking, or test-only route in the named test paths. The Typebot browser routes are explicit unrelated UI doubles, not support for a Meta claim. The Meta and Evolution fakes enforce scoped values and deterministic owned fixture subjects; the current critical adapter assertion runs against MetaHttpClient itself. No silent real-provider fallback, ambient live-data selection, or fake success path was found. The browser evidence is correctly scoped to its fixture backend, not Meta compatibility.

No module contract was superseded by the test-only change.

Failure modes and uncertainty: covered local negatives include revoked/malformed grant shapes, malformed page data, foreign WABA, cursor cycle/oversize/page budget, generic versus typed errors, stale/cancelled/wrong-generation attempts, identity quarantine, tenant ownership, and CSRF. Remaining uncertainty is deliberately material: real Meta semantics and credentials, external callback/runtime behavior, device-level IN/OUT, automatic recovery after interruption, public-origin freshness, and production capacity are unproven. findings.title: External D-06/VAL-05 evidence remains a delivery blocker
findings.rationale:
Why now: the local source and current API leaf cannot prove real Meta authorization, selected official resource behavior, subscription/callback behavior, device IN/OUT, or the already-authorized Evolution recovery. The active TODO records D-06 as Exception and VAL-05 as blocked without a waiver. The package also states that the public origin still serves an older API; this reviewer did not probe it.

Evidence: TODO Decision Adherence Validation and Completion Evidence Matrix; cp36i-result.json; root-cp36i-validation-receipt.json; cp48 readiness evidence. Local doubles, PostgreSQL, and browser fixtures substantiate local behavior only.

Options:
A. Treat the local suite and provider doubles as proof of the external journey and close the delivery. Effort: low; risk/blast radius/maintenance/security impact: unacceptable because it converts simulated compatibility into a release assertion.
B. Record cp36i as a local-source gate only, keep D-06/VAL-05 blocked, and proceed to the distinct final review with the current bounded evidence. Effort: low; risk: controlled; maintenance/elegance/structural impact: preserves the existing truthful gate structure.
C. Complete the authorized real-provider and recovery sequence before any final local gate. Effort: higher and externally dependent; risk reduction: highest, but it need not prevent the bounded final review first.

Recommendation: B now, followed by C for delivery. This is not a request to rerun or waive the same external gate.

findings.title: Freshness composition must not be relabeled as a fresh cross-stack or browser run
findings.rationale:
Why now: cp36i has fresh API evidence only. The source freeze shows exactly one changed file, api-app/src/integrations/meta/meta.client.spec.ts, while the other eight named public paths match cp36h. The historical browser manifests intentionally retain the old unit-spec hash. tsconfig.build.json excludes **/*.spec.ts, so unchanged Web/browser consumer evidence is reusable, but it cannot become a fresh browser or all-suite claim merely by arithmetic.

Options:
A. Report a fresh all-suite/browser result from combined counts. Effort: low; risk: high evidence overstatement; structural/elegance impact: poor.
B. Keep the current wording: fresh API 173-unit plus 288-PG leaf, with historical h Web-28/browser-47 reuse for byte-identical consumer sources. Effort: low; risk: controlled; recommendation: this option.
C. Run a new full browser/cross-stack suite after a future candidate checkpoint. Effort: higher; it provides stronger fresh platform evidence but is unnecessary to validate the spec-only compiled-output-neutral delta itself.

Recommendation: B unless a later gate needs a newly served browser/runtime assertion.
findings.suggested_action: Preserve the original h manifest hashes and explicitly label browser/Web evidence as unchanged-source historical reuse; do not claim a fresh all-suite, fresh browser, or served-cp36i validation.
